title: Admin Assistant- Floyd Lock & Safe
body:
Apply Now 
Admin Assistant- Floyd Lock & Safe
 Per Mar Security Services is seeking a qualified candidate to provide administrative, clerical, and customer service support for the Lock and Safe division of our business, Floyd Lock & Safe. This role supports the daily operations of a busy locksmith business by providing administrative and clerical assistance, including data entry, reporting, work order processing and invoicing, inventory support, customer service, and lock shop assistance. Working with a team serving residential, commercial, and lock shop customers, this position is ideal for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, customer-focused, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Why Per Mar Security? Hourly rate of $20-$24 Opportunity for advancement as the team grows Great Benefit Package including Health, Dental, Vision, Disability, Life, 401K with match, and Paid Time Off Stable company with over 60 years of experience providing security to our communities and continued growth In this role, you will: Provide general administrative support, including answering phones, responding to emails, maintaining databases, and processing administrative documentation. Perform accurate data entry, compile operational information and metrics, and assist with reporting. Generate, process, and invoice customer work orders while ensuring information is accurate and complete. Provide customer service and assist customers with sales, billing, service, and general inquiries. Work directly with walk-in customers in the lock shop to fulfill orders, process billing, and provide a positive customer experience. Assist with inventory management by monitoring stock levels, coordinating replenishment, maintaining inventory records, and processing supply orders. Assist lock technicians as needed to support daily lock shop and field operations. Review customer service information from emails, work orders, and job tickets to ensure accurate and timely processing. Work with department teams, technicians, and management to help resolve daily issues and keep workflows moving efficiently. Maintain accurate records and organized documentation while supporting efficient, customer-focused business operations. Maintain confidentiality while handling sensitive employee, customer, and business information with professionalism. What you’ll need: High school diploma or equivalent required. 1–4 years of relevant clerical, administrative, customer service, or office experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel and Word, and the ability to quickly learn database, inventory management, and other software systems. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong verbal and written communication skills with a customer-focused approach. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work collaboratively with customers, technicians, department teams, and management. Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive employee and customer information with professionalism. Experience in a field service, locksmith, safe, or physical security environment is preferred.     
 Apply Now

 Organize, park, stage, and move vehicles throughout the dealership lot

 Uphold Walser’s Core Values: Do the Right Thing, Lead by Example, Display Positive Energy, and Be Open Minded 
 What You Bring 
 You don’t need years of automotive experience to make an impact here. We’re looking for someone who is dependable, organized, motivated, and ready to contribute. 
 Must be at least 18 years of age 
 Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record 
 Comfortable driving and maneuvering a variety of vehicles 
 Ability and willingness to work outdoors in varying weather conditions 
 Strong organization and time-management skills 
 Attention to detail and ability to keep multiple priorities moving 
 A positive attitude and willingness to jump in where needed 
 A team-first mindset and dependable work ethic 
 Why Join Metropolitan Ford + Walser? 
 You’re joining at an exciting time. Metropolitan Ford is beginning a new chapter as part of Walser Automotive Group, giving you the opportunity to be part of the team we’re building from the start.

title: Office Manager for Property Management Company
body:
Office Manager – Property Management
St. Louis Park, MN | Full-Time
We are a small, established and evolving property management company in St. Louis Park looking for an organized, dependable and personable Office Manager to join our team.
This is a hands-on position in a small office. You will work directly with management, residents, maintenance staff and outside vendors to help keep the day-to-day operations of our apartment portfolio running smoothly. We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their work, communicates well, stays organized when things get busy and is comfortable learning new technology.
Property management experience is preferred but not required. We are willing to train the right person who is capable, organized, comfortable with technology and learns quickly.
Responsibilities
Answer resident phone calls and provide friendly, professional customer service
Enter maintenance work orders and follow up to ensure they are completed and residents are kept informed
Coordinate scheduling between residents, maintenance staff and outside vendors
Obtain bids and help identify competitive vendors for projects and repairs
Receive rent payments, make deposits and accurately post payments to resident ledgers
Assist residents with questions regarding their accounts, leases and building policies
Coordinate resident move-ins and prepare move-in paperwork and packets
Inspect apartments prior to move-in to ensure they are ready for new residents
Enter leases, notices and other documentation into property management software
Manage the lease-renewal process and track upcoming expirations
Prepare and distribute resident notices and communications
Scan and organize incoming mail and property records
Assist with leasing and showing available apartments as needed
Maintain accurate electronic records and resident files
Help identify ways to improve office procedures, resident communication and overall efficiency
Handle other administrative and property-management duties as they arise
What We're Looking For
The right person will be:
Highly organized and able to keep track of multiple tasks at once
Dependable and comfortable taking responsibility for getting things completed
Friendly and professional when dealing with residents and the public
Comfortable handling occasional difficult or frustrated residents
A strong communicator, particularly over the phone
Comfortable using computers, smartphones and web-based software
Able to learn new systems and procedures quickly
Detail-oriented when handling payments, paperwork and resident records
Able to work independently while also being part of a small team
Willing to jump in and solve problems rather than waiting to be told every next step
Experience with property management, leasing, customer service, administrative work or office management is helpful, but we are primarily looking for someone with the right combination of organization, judgment, reliability and willingness to learn.
A valid driver's license is required. Employment is contingent upon satisfactory completion of applicable background screening.
Benefits
We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:
Paid time off
Health insurance
Dental insurance
Vision insurance
Retirement benefits
Paid training and opportunities to grow with the company
If you enjoy working in a small-business environment where your work has a direct impact and you're looking for a position with variety and responsibility, we'd like to hear from you.
To apply, please submit your resume along with a brief introduction about yourself and why you think you would be a good fit for this position.

title: Office Support
body:
About Precision Tree
We are the premier tree removal service in the Metro dedicated to safety, efficiency, and quality work. Our crew is made up of hard-working, no-nonsense individuals who are experts in their field. We offer a fast-paced, results-driven, and straight-shooting culture—think less corporate cubicle, and more hardworking, locker-room camaraderie. We need a highly organized self-starter to be the vital administrative center that keeps our operational wheels turning.
The Role: Office Assistant
You will be the core of our office, ensuring that our estimators and management team can focus on the field. This role requires exceptional attention to detail, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to manage multiple high-priority tasks simultaneously.
Key Responsibilities
· Front Line Communication: Answer and direct all incoming phone calls efficiently and professionally.
· Administrative Management: Handle all data entry, organize documents, and manage physical and digital filing systems.
· Financial Support: Assist with billing processes, tracking invoices, and basic financial documentation.
· Compliance & Permits: Manage applications for necessary permits and licenses to ensure team compliance.
· Supply Chain: Maintain and order all office supplies and essential materials, ensuring stock levels are always adequate.
· Team Support: Directly assist estimators with documentation, scheduling, and project preparation.
· Management Support: Provide administrative assistance to all levels of management as needed.
Qualifications & Must-Haves
· Experience: 1+ years of experience in an office or administrative support role (preferred).
· Technical Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and CRM software.
· Organizational Mastery: Exceptional attention to detail is non-negotiable. Must be highly effective at time management and 
 prioritize a heavy workload
· Initiative: Must be a proactive self-starter with strong problem-solving skills—we need someone who anticipates needs and
 tackles
 tasks without constant direction
· Grit: The ability to thrive in a high-energy, direct communication environment.
 Compensation & Benefits
We value our team and offer a strong benefits package:
· Competitive wage of approximately $22.00 per hour.

title: Office and Accounting Manager - Construction
body:
Office & Accounting Manager – Construction
Full-Time | Little Canada, Minnesota
Salary: $85,000–$100,000 per year + Performance Bonus
We are a growing small general contracting company seeking an experienced Office & Accounting Manager to take ownership of our accounting, payroll, job costing, HR administration, insurance administration, and subcontractor compliance functions.
This is a key position within our company. We are looking for someone who understands that running the back office of a construction company involves much more than bookkeeping. You will work directly with the owner and project management team and will be responsible for keeping the financial and administrative side of the business accurate, organized, current and running smoothly.
The ideal candidate has previous construction accounting experience, is highly proficient with QuickBooks Online, understands job costing, and is comfortable independently managing everything from payroll and customer billing to subcontractor insurance certificates and W-9s.
If you are the person who notices when something doesn’t reconcile, follows up when paperwork is missing, and doesn’t need to be reminded three times to get something done, we would like to talk with you.
Compensation & Benefits
Base Salary: $85,000–$100,000, depending on experience and qualifications
Performance Bonus: Up to 10% of annual salary based on achievement of established performance goals
Benefits may include:
• Paid time off
• Paid holidays
• Health insurance contribution
• 401(k) with company match
• Dental and vision insurance
• Life and disability insurance
• Mileage reimbursement for authorized business travel
• Continuing education and professional training
Primary Responsibilities
Accounting & Financial Management
• Manage day-to-day accounting using QuickBooks Online
• Process and manage accounts payable and accounts receivable
• Prepare and issue customer invoices and progress billings
• Monitor accounts receivable and actively follow up on past-due accounts
• Review, code and enter vendor and subcontractor invoices
• Ensure invoices are properly approved before payment
• Reconcile bank accounts and credit cards monthly
• Maintain an accurate general ledger
• Assist with monthly and year-end accounting close
• Work directly with the company’s outside CPA/accounting firm
• Prepare financial and management reports for the owner
Construction Job Costing
• Maintain accurate job-cost records for each construction project
• Properly allocate labor, materials, subcontractors and other costs to individual jobs
• Review job costs for accuracy and identify unusual or improperly coded expenses
• Prepare project profitability and job-cost reports for management
• Assist project managers with monitoring actual costs versus budgets
• Help ensure change orders, deposits and additional work are properly documented and billed
Payroll & Timekeeping
• Process payroll accurately and on schedule
• Review employee timecards for completeness and accuracy
• Ensure employee labor is charged to the correct jobs and cost categories
• Maintain payroll records and employee deductions
• Process expense reimbursements
• Coordinate payroll tax and reporting matters with outside providers as necessary
HR & Employee Administration
• Maintain confidential employee personnel files
• Coordinate new-employee onboarding and payroll setup
• Maintain employee tax forms and benefit documentation
• Assist with employee benefit administration
• Process compensation and employment-status changes
• Assist management with employee documentation and personnel matters
• Coordinate administrative requirements associated with employee departures and terminations
• Maintain required employment records and assist with Minnesota leave and employment compliance
Insurance & Workers’ Compensation
• Maintain company insurance records
• Coordinate with the company’s insurance broker
• Assist with general liability, commercial auto, property, umbrella and workers’ compensation renewals
• Maintain workers’ compensation payroll and classification information
• Assist with workers’ compensation audits
• Coordinate administrative documentation following workplace injuries
• Maintain required incident and insurance documentation
Subcontractor & Vendor Compliance
• Obtain and maintain Form W-9s from subcontractors and vendors
• Maintain information required for year-end 1099 reporting
• Obtain and track subcontractor Certificates of Insurance
• Monitor expiration dates for subcontractor insurance coverage
• Maintain executed subcontractor agreements
• Verify required subcontractor paperwork is received before work begins or payments are released
• Maintain organized subcontractor and vendor files
• Follow up aggressively on missing or expired documentation
Office & Administrative Management
• Maintain organized electronic accounting, project and administrative records
• Develop and maintain written office procedures
• Coordinate administrative workflow with the owner, project managers and field employees
• Assist with company registrations, licenses and other administrative compliance requirements
• Identify administrative problems before they become larger problems
• Recommend improvements to accounting and office procedures
• Perform other administrative and accounting responsibilities as reasonably assigned
Qualifications
Required:
• Minimum 5–7 years of accounting, bookkeeping or office financial-management experience
• Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks Online
• Significant accounts payable and accounts receivable experience
• Payroll-processing experience
• Strong understanding of bank and credit-card reconciliations
• Strong Microsoft Excel skills
• Excellent organizational and follow-up skills
• Strong attention to detail
• Ability to manage multiple deadlines
• Ability to work independently with limited supervision
• Ability to handle confidential employee and financial information
Strongly Preferred:
• Previous experience working for a general contractor, subcontractor or construction company
• Construction job-cost accounting experience
• Experience working with subcontractors
• Experience administering W-9s, 1099s and Certificates of Insurance
• Workers’ compensation and business-insurance experience
• Experience working with outside CPAs and payroll providers
• Experience with construction or project-management software
An accounting or business degree is helpful but not required. We place significant value on practical construction accounting and office-management experience.
Who We’re Looking For
We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their work.
You may be a particularly good fit if you are the person who:
• Notices when the numbers don’t make sense
• Wants to know why a job is over budget
• Doesn’t pay an invoice simply because someone submitted it
• Tracks down missing receipts instead of ignoring them
• Follows up on overdue customer invoices
• Makes sure subcontractor insurance hasn’t expired
• Keeps payroll and job costing accurate
• Creates a system when there isn’t one
• Can politely but persistently get information from busy project managers and field employees
• Understands that accurate accounting is essential to running a profitable construction company
This is not simply a bookkeeping position and it is not simply an administrative assistant position. It is a hands-on management position responsible for helping keep the financial and administrative side of a construction company under control.
Schedule
Full-time, Monday through Friday
This is primarily an office-based position requiring regular interaction with ownership, project managers, employees, vendors and subcontractors.
Compensation
$85,000–$100,000 per year, depending upon relevant construction, accounting and management experience, plus the opportunity to earn an annual performance bonus of up to 10% of base salary.
We are an equal opportunity employer and consider qualified applicants without regard to protected characteristics under applicable federal, state and local law.

title: Accounting Manager (New site)
body:
Apply Now New Accounting Manager position! 
Mendota Heights, Minnesota 
 Join us as we build something new! 
 CPP is preparing to open a new manufacturing site in Mendota Heights, Minnesota , and we are looking for an experienced Accounting Manager to join our team and play a key role in establishing and supporting the financial operations of this new facility. 
 This is an exciting opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys working in a manufacturing environment, partnering with operations, and using financial information to drive business performance. The Accounting Manager will work closely with the Controller and site leadership to ensure accurate financial reporting, strong internal controls, GAAP compliance, and meaningful financial analysis.
 What You'll Do 
 Manage general accounting functions and prepare financial reports and statistics reflecting earnings, profits, cash balances, weekly metrics, and other financial results using the Oracle ERP system and other resources. 
 Ensure proper setup and accounting of all fixed assets and coordinate with Corporate Finance to provide reports for audits, depreciation schedules, financial reporting, and corporate analysis. 
 Coordinate, review, assemble, and distribute daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting in partnership with the Controller. 
 Prepare and interpret financial analysis of profit and loss and balance sheet accounts and present findings to the Controller. 
 Serve as a key financial partner to the Controller and site leadership by providing real-time visibility into department and manufacturing performance to help drive productivity and continuous improvement. 
 Ensure GAAP compliance within the General Ledger through account reconciliations, accuracy reviews, and timely identification and communication of issues. 
 Analyze financial statements and identify discrepancies, trends, and other issues requiring the Controller's attention. 
 Partner with Purchasing and other functional teams to manage capital projects, including ROI analysis, spending reviews, and ensuring projects are completed on time and within budget. 
 Perform monthly analysis of account accruals and prepaid expenses. 
 Identify and lead continuous improvement initiatives related to finance and accounting processes. 
 Partner with IT to develop and implement applications, systems, and tools that support the Finance and Accounting organization. 
 Assist with year-end and quarterly physical inventory processes. 
 Assist with year-end close activities and the Cost Roll process. 
 Produce and distribute key financial indicator reports to executive management. 
 Act as a liaison with sales and use tax and state income tax auditors, providing accurate information and supporting analysis. 
 Provide accurate and timely information and assistance to independent auditors to support the efficient completion of the annual audit. 
 Provide backup support across Finance, including accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, and cost accounting functions. 
 What We're Looking For 
 Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance. 
 3-6 years of progressive accounting experience, preferably within a publicly traded manufacturing environment. 
 Strong understanding of GAAP, general ledger accounting, financial reporting, and account reconciliations. 
 Experience with ERP systems (Oracle) and financial reporting tools. 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate financial data into actionable business insights. 
 Experience with fixed assets, inventory, accruals, prepaids, capital projects, and cost accounting. 
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to financial accuracy. 
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet reporting deadlines in a fast-paced environment. 
 Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to partner effectively with Finance, Operations, Purchasing, IT, Sales, and Corporate teams. 
 Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities for process improvement and lead projects through implementation. 
 Experience supporting internal and external audits is preferred. 
 CPA or other professional accounting designation is a plus. 
 Why Join CPP? 
 Be part of building a new operation from the ground up. 
 The Accounting Manager will have a unique opportunity to help establish financial processes, systems, reporting, and controls for a brand-new manufacturing site. Your work will have a direct impact on the success of the facility and will provide meaningful exposure to site leadership and Corporate Finance. 
 If you are a hands-on accounting professional who enjoys manufacturing, financial analysis, operational partnership, and continuous improvement , we want to hear from you.
 What We Offer 
 $120-135,000 annual salary 
 5% quarterly bonus potential 
 Onsite flexible schedule  
 Paid training & educational assistance to grow your career 
 Health, dental, vision insurance available the 1st of the following month after you start 
 401(k) with company match 
 PTO and ESST paid time off 
 A collaborative, team-driven culture where your contributions matter

More information about our company can be found at: http://www.cppcorp.com/ .

• Continuing education and professional training
Primary Responsibilities
Accounting & Financial Management
• Manage day-to-day accounting using QuickBooks Online
• Process and manage accounts payable and accounts receivable
• Prepare and issue customer invoices and progress billings
• Monitor accounts receivable and actively follow up on past-due accounts
• Review, code and enter vendor and subcontractor invoices
• Ensure invoices are properly approved before payment
• Reconcile bank accounts and credit cards monthly
• Maintain an accurate general ledger
• Assist with monthly and year-end accounting close
• Work directly with the company’s outside CPA/accounting firm
• Prepare financial and management reports for the owner
Construction Job Costing
• Maintain accurate job-cost records for each construction project
• Properly allocate labor, materials, subcontractors and other costs to individual jobs
• Review job costs for accuracy and identify unusual or improperly coded expenses
• Prepare project profitability and job-cost reports for management
• Assist project managers with monitoring actual costs versus budgets
• Help ensure change orders, deposits and additional work are properly documented and billed
Payroll & Timekeeping
• Process payroll accurately and on schedule
• Review employee timecards for completeness and accuracy
• Ensure employee labor is charged to the correct jobs and cost categories
• Maintain payroll records and employee deductions
• Process expense reimbursements
• Coordinate payroll tax and reporting matters with outside providers as necessary
HR & Employee Administration
• Maintain confidential employee personnel files
• Coordinate new-employee onboarding and payroll setup
• Maintain employee tax forms and benefit documentation
• Assist with employee benefit administration
• Process compensation and employment-status changes
• Assist management with employee documentation and personnel matters
• Coordinate administrative requirements associated with employee departures and terminations
• Maintain required employment records and assist with Minnesota leave and employment compliance
Insurance & Workers’ Compensation
• Maintain company insurance records
• Coordinate with the company’s insurance broker
• Assist with general liability, commercial auto, property, umbrella and workers’ compensation renewals
• Maintain workers’ compensation payroll and classification information
• Assist with workers’ compensation audits
• Coordinate administrative documentation following workplace injuries
• Maintain required incident and insurance documentation
Subcontractor & Vendor Compliance
• Obtain and maintain Form W-9s from subcontractors and vendors
• Maintain information required for year-end 1099 reporting
• Obtain and track subcontractor Certificates of Insurance
• Monitor expiration dates for subcontractor insurance coverage
• Maintain executed subcontractor agreements
• Verify required subcontractor paperwork is received before work begins or payments are released
• Maintain organized subcontractor and vendor files
• Follow up aggressively on missing or expired documentation
Office & Administrative Management
• Maintain organized electronic accounting, project and administrative records
• Develop and maintain written office procedures
• Coordinate administrative workflow with the owner, project managers and field employees
• Assist with company registrations, licenses and other administrative compliance requirements
• Identify administrative problems before they become larger problems
• Recommend improvements to accounting and office procedures
• Perform other administrative and accounting responsibilities as reasonably assigned
Qualifications
Required:
• Minimum 5–7 years of accounting, bookkeeping or office financial-management experience
• Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks Online
• Significant accounts payable and accounts receivable experience
• Payroll-processing experience
• Strong understanding of bank and credit-card reconciliations
• Strong Microsoft Excel skills
• Excellent organizational and follow-up skills
• Strong attention to detail
• Ability to manage multiple deadlines
• Ability to work independently with limited supervision
• Ability to handle confidential employee and financial information
Strongly Preferred:
• Previous experience working for a general contractor, subcontractor or construction company
• Construction job-cost accounting experience
• Experience working with subcontractors
• Experience administering W-9s, 1099s and Certificates of Insurance
• Workers’ compensation and business-insurance experience
• Experience working with outside CPAs and payroll providers
• Experience with construction or project-management software
An accounting or business degree is helpful but not required. We place significant value on practical construction accounting and office-management experience.
Who We’re Looking For
We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their work.
You may be a particularly good fit if you are the person who:
• Notices when the numbers don’t make sense
• Wants to know why a job is over budget
• Doesn’t pay an invoice simply because someone submitted it
• Tracks down missing receipts instead of ignoring them
• Follows up on overdue customer invoices
• Makes sure subcontractor insurance hasn’t expired
• Keeps payroll and job costing accurate
• Creates a system when there isn’t one
• Can politely but persistently get information from busy project managers and field employees
• Understands that accurate accounting is essential to running a profitable construction company
This is not simply a bookkeeping position and it is not simply an administrative assistant position. It is a hands-on management position responsible for helping keep the financial and administrative side of a construction company under control.
Schedule
Full-time, Monday through Friday
This is primarily an office-based position requiring regular interaction with ownership, project managers, employees, vendors and subcontractors.
Compensation
$85,000–$100,000 per year, depending upon relevant construction, accounting and management experience, plus the opportunity to earn an annual performance bonus of up to 10% of base salary.
We are an equal opportunity employer and consider qualified applicants without regard to protected characteristics under applicable federal, state and local law.

title: Client Service Leader
body:
Apply Now Introduction 
 At Gallagher Benefit Services, you’re a trusted partner to organizations navigating some of their most important people decisions. We help clients build better workplaces, where people feel supported, empowered, and inspired to thrive. Whether it’s shaping benefit strategies, designing wellbeing programs, or advising on workforce challenges, the work you do here creates meaningful change for businesses and the people who power them.  We’re a community of bold explorers, trusted experts, and compassionate partners; working side by side to solve problems, and shape the future of work. Here, curiosity is encouraged, collaboration is second nature, and your ideas have room to grow.  If you’re looking for a place where your contribution matters and where you can help build a better world of work; think of Gallagher.   
 Overview 
 As the  Client Service Leader  you will ensure delivery of exceptional service to Gallagher’s clients by managing our client service teams. You will champion branch initiatives and drive our dominant priorities. You will use your experience in client service and business insight to lead our team and create depth in our client relationships. We will look to you to develop and cultivate outstanding relationships within our branch and with our clients and vendor partners. 
 How you'll make an impact 
 You monitor overall book and client assignments for the team while managing 1-2 clients to keep you in touch with the marketplace Providing guidance in the employee benefits Client Service Cycle to ensure a seamless renewal process and handle advanced service issues. We measure success based on retention and our renewal target is 95% You continuously assess the performance of team members. You provide ongoing, timely feedback and coaching to improve performance Prioritizing team workflow and ensure accountability and compliance in both internal and external partnerships Communicating performance expectations and ensure team members have the resources to achieve their goals You recognize the client strategy and can determine appropriate coverage solutions that support and enhance the clients' culture, values, and mission You support consultants in winning new business by participating in meetings and calls with prospects and effectively communicating Gallagher’s Value Proposition You encourage "cross-solving" with clients to communicate resources available within Gallagher that we may not currently provide (Pharmacy Practice, Retirement Services, HR Consulting, Voluntary Benefits, etc.) and actively seek business referrals You champion Gallagher resources and tools to maximize efficiency in managing client deliverables Guiding, developing, and mentoring new hires, account management, and team resources and foster team engagement by supporting our culture and driving commitment to the Gallagher Way Complete internal professional development programs to gain an understanding of the insurance industry and GBS processes We ask our team to exemplify the highest ethical standards, promote ethical behavior and uphold The Gallagher Way What skills will make me successful in this role? You are comfortable giving and receiving constructive feedback Demonstrating a high level of professionalism in all interactions You recognize each teammate is unique and seek to learn their unique goals and priorities You have navigated the benefits market from the broker perspective, the renewal cycle, and the financial drivers that impact our clients You take action to influence events, achieve team goals, and retain clients Adaptable and remain composed and in an environment that requires balancing multiple priorities in any given day You actively seek to develop your professional skills and improve efficiency and productivity You are innovative and rarely satisfied with the status quo. You love to generate new and practical ideas and aim to continuously improve You have a desire to build a knowledge of Gallagher tools, systems and shared resources We look for the people who go the “Extra Mile” to achieve results that benefit the client, the Branch and Gallagher 
 About You 
 Required: Bachelor's degree with 5+ years client service and/or claims management experience -OR- High School degree/GED with 10+ years client service and/or claims management experience. 1+ years supervisory experience. Appropriate licensing as required Preferred: Prior experience designing and implementing productivity and client service improvements Experience leading and managing teams (preferably within a matrix environment) within an operational service delivery or shared services environment Keen understanding of professional and industry standards/practices. 
#LI-TW2 
 Compensation and benefits 
 At Gallagher, we believe supporting our colleagues goes far beyond the role itself. For more information, visit our Benefits page . Competitive compensation Comprehensive benefits programs designed to support your well-being  Career development opportunities and ongoing learning  A collaborative, people-first culture with accessible leadership  The opportunity to do meaningful work with global reach and local impact  At Gallagher, we are dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace. If your past experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to join our Talent Community to stay connected to additional career opportunities. At times, we will consider transferable skills from previous roles. Gallagher is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer (Minorities/Females/Veterans/Disabled) Apply Now

title: Blue-Collar Talent Scout (Work From Home)
body:
We're looking for someone who's part recruiter, part talent scout, part network builder, and who understands or can relate to how blue-collar contractors think. 
This is NOT a typical recruiting position. We're looking for someone who believes they can, by themselves, hunt down people interested in working with us as subcontractors during the winter months in the roofing sector. You also need to be someone who has, or can quickly grasp, a very basic understanding of the roofing trade. 
Our company has been in business for 33 years, is an industry leader in the roofing sector, operates nationwide, and relies on a large network of independent contractors. Our challenge isn't finding customers. Our challenge is finding enough great roofing technicians to meet demand.
That's where you come in.
Your mission is simple: build the largest, highest-quality network possible of contractors interested in working with us during the winter months.
We're not looking for someone who sits back and waits for resumes to come in; that won't happen. We're looking for someone who wakes up wondering..."Where or how can I find some more great people today - somewhere that nobody else is looking?"
If you call me in a week and say "I found an entirely new source of candidates that nobody else had thought of," you'll probably make my day. If five months from now, you've built a nationwide pipeline of reliable roofing technicians who are eager to work with us in the winter, you've succeeded.
You'll have the freedom to experiment and think outside the box. Buy email lists. Create Craigslist ads. Write email campaigns. Search Facebook groups. Contact associations. Reach out to industry organizations. Build referral networks. Call previous candidates. Develop systems. We'll support reasonable recruiting ideas and tools if you can make a case for them.
I'm not looking for someone to simply follow a script. There is no script! I'm looking for someone who wants to use their own head to craft new ways to find qualified & interested roofing technicians. 
The ideal person MUST be:
• Excellent on the phone
• Comfortable talking with complete strangers
• Creative and resourceful
• Self-motivated and self-directed
• Organized and persistent
• Curious about finding new recruiting opportunities
• Someone who enjoys building relationships and connecting people with opportunities
• Trustworthy (must be trustworthy)
• Construction or roofing experience is absolutely not necessary, but it would be a *HUGE* bonus
This is a remote position. You can live anywhere in the United States.
This position is temporary and part-time (likely from September through February). There is flexibility in the schedule, and if you prove yourself, there's no reason this opportunity couldn't continue well beyond one season. Also, if you prove yourself (e.g., results!) the flexibility of your hours, days, etc. could be endless. 
Compensation will include hourly pay, along with potential commissions.
When you reply, please tell me in great detail:
• Why you think you'd be good at this position.
• Your background in sales, recruiting, networking, business development, if any.
• An example of a creative way you've found customers, employees, or opportunities, if any. 
• Where you're located.
• Your compensation expectations. 
• Anything else you think I should know.
Please read this *entire* ad. Please be detailed in your reply. I enjoy reading thoughtful, lengthy replies. Short replies or replies including only a resume will be ignored. I'm looking for someone who is fired up about this opportunity! 
Joe

title: Rare Epilepsy Market Lead - Midwest
body:
Apply Now Territory   – Midwest 
 Target cities within the territory include Minneapolis, Denver, Kansas City, and Iowa City.  The Midwest territory includes portions of Colorado, Nebraska, Iowa, Missouri, and Minnesota. 
 The Rare Epilepsy Market Lead is a strategic, field-based leader and local market expert responsible for engaging with key epilepsy Centers of Excellence (COEs) and rare epilepsy HCP treaters to identify barriers to treatment and provide appropriate disease state education while serving as a trusted resource for healthcare professionals seeking information  related to Onfi® (clobazam) and Sabril® (vigabatrin) consistent with applicable compliance requirements. 
 Further, this role will be responsible for generating actionable insights, identifying local market opportunities, and compliant coordination with cross-functional stakeholders across Commercial, Medical, Advocacy, and Market Access as appropriate to strengthen disease awareness, patient understanding, and education across the ecosystem to advance Lundbeck’s mission to improve the lives of people living with rare and serious neurological conditions. 
 PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Serve as the primary local market expert, continuously assessing customer preferences and patient needs, treatment dynamics, access challenges, competitive activity, and emerging opportunities across the rare epilepsy ecosystem. 
 Develop and execute a comprehensive territory business plan aligned to national strategy while tailoring execution to local market dynamics. 
 Appropriately identify field-driven innovative solutions, including deployment models and executional plans based on local market dynamics, while maintaining alignment to BU strategies. 
 Provide appropriate education and educational resources on Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathies (DEEs) and seizure disorders, including disease identification, patient journey, treatment considerations, and appropriate use of Onfi® and Sabril® when requested 
 Bridge local insights and enterprise strategy by leveraging a deep understanding of local epilepsy COEs, and treatment ecosystems to inform appropriate coordinated account engagement 
 Develop awareness of, and appropriately engage with, local and regional patient advocacy organizations to support disease education, community engagement, and patient-centric initiatives in a compliant manner 
 Demonstrate intellectual curiosity and a continuous learning mindset to uncover the underlying drivers of market dynamics and customer behavior 
 Develop integrated account strategies that leverage the appropriate expertise and resources across Lundbeck to address complex challenges 
 Appropriately operate as part of broader cross-functional organization and with other internal stakeholders, to ensure customer interactions are coordinated, purposeful, and aligned with account priorities and patient needs and broader commercial strategy 
 In the future, potential to be responsible for management of, and collaboration across, a field-based team 
 Utilize business analytics and CRM tools to track territory activity, account insights, and progress against business objectives 
 Foster teamwork and a collaborative culture, champion and role model our Lundbeck rare epilepsy ways of working by empowering team members, acting with urgency, and orchestrating our customer experience to benefit the rare epilepsy patients and families we serve 
 Ability to understand sophisticated reimbursement and distribution processes in a complex coverage landscape. Anticipates and appropriately communicates coverage changes to stakeholders 
 Ability to apply knowledge of pharmaceutical and regulatory environment, including Lundbeck policies and procedures and FDA regulations regarding the promotion of pharmaceutical and medical products 
 Accountability and adherence to corporate, FDA, and PDMA guidelines 
 REQUIREMENTS 
 Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university 
 7+ years' experience in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry 
 3+ years of specialty sales experience in pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, biologics, medical device sales or related healthcare sales experience.  Demonstrated track record of performance in a complex, low-volume, high-science selling environment 
 Ownership and accountability for the development and execution of fully integrated account plans 
 Strong clinical and business acumen with the ability to engage credibly in scientific and medical discussions with specialist-level customers and key stakeholders across epilepsy centers 
 Excellent communication, organizational, and cross-functional collaboration skills 
 Strong understanding of patient and caregivers needs, purpose-driven with a demonstrated commitment to patient-centric engagement 
 Demonstrated curiosity, adaptability and entrepreneurial mindset consistent with a lean, results-oriented commercial organization 
 Self-directed with the ability to operate and thrive as an individual contributor with a mindset that embraces evolution & change 
 Meeting and complying with reasonable industry-standard credentialing requirements of healthcare providers / customer facilities is required for continued employment with Lundbeck  
 Driving is an essential duty of this job; must have a valid driver’s license in good standing. 
 Must live within a state in the Midwest territory or be state adjacent.  
 The role is part of Lundbeck’s Vehicle Fleet Stipend Program and requires business use of a personal vehicle. More information on the stipend program can be found  here

 A strong-performing division of Green Bay Packaging is looking for a leader to build on an already successful operation and drive the next level of strategic growth. You’ll lead four diverse teams bringing alignment, accountability, and collaboration across the business to unlock the next level of performance.

 Partner with the President/GM to develop and execute commercial strategies that drive divisional results.

 Lead, develop, and engage Sales, Design, and Customer Service teams through coaching, mentoring, and performance accountability.

 Improve margins through disciplined pricing strategy, negotiations, and cross-functional alignment. 
 Facilitate sales meetings and represent the organization at customer events (including occasional evenings/weekends). 
 Maintain strong knowledge of GBP corrugated product offerings and competitive solutions. 
 We’re looking for a leader who is hungry, humble, and smart—someone who builds teams, develops people, and drives results. 
 Qualifications 
 5+ years of progressive success in direct sales, including significant experience opening new accounts. 
 Proven ability to lead and manage teams across multiple functions while balancing competing priorities. 
 Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field required. 
 Demonstrated leadership capabilities with strong coaching, development, and motivational skills. 
 Strong commercial background with solid business acumen and financial understanding. 
 Knowledge of the corrugated or packaging industry strongly preferred.

 Started in 1933, Green Bay Packaging Inc. is a family owned, vertically integrated company consisting of corrugated container plants, a folding carton facility, recycled and virgin containerboard mills, pressure-sensitive label roll stock plants, timberlands, a paper slitting operation, and a sawmill facility. Headquartered in Green Bay, Wis., Green Bay Packaging Inc. employs over 4,600 team members and operates 40 facilities in 16 states, each with a dedication to innovative development of its products and forestry resources, with a focus on safety, sustainability, quality, and continuous improvement. title: B2B Service Company Sales & Customer Account Rep
body:
Sales & Customer Account Representative
We are an established B2B service company serving businesses throughout Minnesota and Western WI. We have a competitive market advantage in and outside of the areas we provide service. Our growth comes from this and building strong relationships, delivering reliable service, and earning repeat business from our customers.
We're looking for a driven, personable Sales & Customer Account Representative to help grow the company. This is a sales-focused position for someone who enjoys talking with business decision makers, developing relationships, finding opportunities, and closing.
About the Position:
Your primary responsibility will be generating new business and growing existing accounts.
You'll spend your time identifying prospects, making calls, following up on leads, meeting with customers, presenting our services, preparing proposals, and asking for the sale. You'll also serve as a key point of contact for existing customers and look for opportunities to expand those relationships.
This is a hands-on sales role in a small-company environment. We need someone who is comfortable picking up the phone, creating opportunities, following up consistently, and taking ownership of the sales process from prospecting through close.
Key Responsibilities:
Prospect for new B2B customers through outbound calls, email, networking, referrals, and other sales activities
Build and maintain a consistent sales pipeline
Identify decision-makers and develop relationships with business owners and managers
Make outbound sales calls and conduct follow-up with prospective customers
Qualify leads and determine customer needs
Present our services and communicate the value we provide
Prepare quotes, proposals, and sales presentations
Follow up consistently and move prospects through the sales process
Close new accounts and meet established sales goals
Develop existing accounts and identify opportunities for additional services
Ask for referrals and generate new opportunities from existing customers
Maintain accurate sales activity and customer information
Stay engaged with customers after the sale to ensure satisfaction and encourage retention
Work closely with operations to ensure a smooth transition from sale to service
Represent the company professionally in the Minnesota business community
What We're Looking For:
The ideal candidate is competitive, persistent, confident, and genuinely enjoys selling.
We're looking for someone who:
Is comfortable making outbound calls and initiating conversations
Isn't afraid to ask for the sale
Can handle rejection and keep prospecting
Has strong follow-up and organizational skills
Builds rapport quickly with business customers
Can identify customer needs and connect them to solutions
Communicates clearly and professionally
Takes ownership of results rather than waiting for leads to appear
Is motivated by goals, achievement, and earning potential
Can work independently while being part of a small team
Has a professional, positive, and dependable attitude
B2B sales, account management, business development, or service-industry experience is preferred, but we will consider candidates with strong sales ability and the right attitude.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this position is measured by new customers, revenue growth, account growth, and consistent sales activity.
We're looking for someone who will actively create opportunities—not someone who waits for the phone to ring.
You should be comfortable setting goals, making the calls necessary to reach them, following up when others don't, and turning conversations into customers.
What We Offer
Base compensation of 40K-50K per year (based on experience)
Sales commission/bonus opportunity: 10K-60K per year (based on sales)
Established customer base and territory
Training on our services and sales process
Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a small company
Direct access to company leadership
Growth opportunities as the company grows
Health disbursement program
Paid time off
Mileage reimbursement, Company vehicle available after 6 months on the job.
Ready to Grow With Us?
If you're a self-motivated salesperson who likes building relationships, winning new business, and seeing the direct results of your work, we'd like to hear from you.
Please submit your resume and a brief introduction explaining your sales experience and why you'd be a good fit for our team.

You’ll be backed by our digital ecosystem: a client-centric suite of consulting tools making it easier for you to meet your clients where they want to be met. Advanced data and analytics providing a comprehensive overview of the risk landscape is at your fingertips.  Here, you’re not just improving clients' risk profiles, you’re building trust. You’ll find a culture grounded in teamwork, guided by integrity, and fueled by a shared commitment to do the right thing. We value curiosity, celebrate new ideas, and empower you to take ownership of your career while making a meaningful impact for the businesses we serve.  If you’re ready to bring your unique perspective to a place where your work truly matters; think of Gallagher.   
 Overview 
 NIS , now part of Gallagher, is seeking an Account Coordinator to join our growing team! This is a hybrid position based out of our Brookfield office in Wisconsin.     Are you highly organized, detail-oriented, and passionate about supporting a dynamic sales team? We're looking for an Account Coordinator to play a critical role in helping our sales and account management teams deliver exceptional employee benefits solutions to clients.   In this role, you'll be the engine behind the proposal and marketing process, partnering with Sales Representatives, Account Representatives, Regional Vice Presidents, carriers, General Agents, and underwriting teams to bring competitive benefit solutions to market. From coordinating carrier quotes and managing proposal timelines to preparing impactful benefit comparisons and supporting sales strategy, your work will directly contribute to winning business and strengthening client relationships.   This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where attention to detail, problem-solving, and relationship-building are key to success.   Why You'll Love This Role: Be a key contributor to a high-performing sales organization. Work closely with leadership, sales professionals, underwriting teams, and carrier partners. Gain exposure to complex employee benefits strategies and market solutions. Make a measurable impact on new business growth and client success. Join a collaborative team that values partnership, innovation, and professional development. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy bringing people and processes together, and take pride in delivering exceptional service, we'd love to hear from you. 
 How you'll make an impact 
 Coordinate and manage the employee benefits proposal, marketing, and bid process from initial request through final submission. Prepare bid specifications for existing clients and review information for prospective opportunities. Serve as a key point of contact between sales teams, carriers, General Agents, underwriting partners, and internal stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate proposal delivery. Gather, organize, and distribute census data, claims experience, questionnaires, bid specifications, and other supporting documents to carrier partners. Track proposal activity and proactively follow up with carriers to obtain quotes, illustrations, underwriting requirements, and supporting materials. Review carrier proposals and prepare side-by-side comparisons to support sales strategy and client presentations. title: Delivery Driver
body:
Apply Now Job Description: Position Details: CDL A License Required Pay:  Once fully trained, drivers average $100,000 a year annually!  Schedule:  Primarily a 4 day work week within Monday through Friday with an occasional 5th day as needed. Drivers have early morning start times. Start and end times vary. Drivers average 10-12/hr days.  $12,000 Sign-on Bonus!   Terms Apply -  Any person who has worked for a Performance Food Group (PFG) owned company within the last 6 months is not eligible to receive this incentive. Drivers dispatch from our Rogers location at 13400 Commerce Blvd.  
 We Deliver the Goods: Competitive pay and benefits, including Day 1 Health & Wellness Benefits, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, 401K Employer Matching, Education Assistance, Paid Time Off, and much more Growth opportunities performing essential work to support America’s food distribution system Safe and inclusive working environment, including culture of rewards, recognition, and respect Position Purpose: 
Food and food service delivery drivers fulfill a critical role in the country’s food supply chain. Our delivery drivers not only make sure the customers’ products arrive at their destination at the arranged times and in good condition, but they are the face of our company – building lasting relationships with our customers!
The CDL-A Driver is responsible for driving a tractor trailer or straight truck on intrastate and interstate local, over-the-road (OTR), shuttle, and overnight and drive and drop routes for the purpose of delivering and/or unloading food and food related products to customers in a safe and timely manner and in accordance with Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations.
 Primary Responsibilities: Communicates and interacts with customers, vendors and co-workers professionally ensuring questions are answered accurately and in a timely manner. Functions as a team member within the department and organization, as required, and perform any duty assigned to best serve the company. Performs all required safety checks (i.e., pre/post trip) including inspections of tractor/truck and trailer according to Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations; inspects tractor/truck and trailer to insure they meet company safety standards and take appropriate action as needed. Reports all safety issues and/or repairs required. Follows all DOT regulations and company safe driving guidelines and policies. Immediately reports all safety hazards. Inspects trailer for properly loaded and secured freight. Performs count check of items and check customer invoices of products that have been loaded. Checks and completes in an accurate and in legible fashion all required paperwork associated with freight. Moves tractor to the loading dock and attach preloaded trailer as needed. Drives to and delivers customer orders according to predetermined route delivery schedule. Unloads products from the trailer, transports items into designated customer storage areas. Performs damage control checks on items, scans, and contact supervisor about removing orders according to company policy. Verifies delivery of items with customer and obtain proper signatures. Collects money (cash or checks) where required. Loads customer returns on to trailer and secures trailer doors. Ensures that tractor, trailer, and freight are appropriately locked and/or always secured. Unloads damaged goods and customer returns and bring to the driver check-in and complete necessary paperwork. Unloads all equipment, materials and remove trash from trailers as required. Completes daily record of hours of service and enter in log in accordance with Federal DOT, state, and company requirements. Performs general housekeeping duties in tractor, loading dock area and keep trailers clear and clean as required. At the end of the shift secure all equipment and complete all necessary paperwork. Performs other related duties as assigned.  Qualifications: High School Diploma/GED
• 6+ months commercial driving
• Valid CDL-A
• Must be 21+ years of age
• Meet all State licensing and/or certification requirements (where applicable)
• Clean Motor Vehicle Report (MVR) for past 3 years
• Pass post offer drug test and criminal background check
• Pass road test
• Attains or has valid current DOT Health Card and/or able to secure new DOT Health Card
• Able to hand-lift and utilize two-wheeler, lift gate and/or other equipment to move and/or stack product cases/freight of varying size and weight throughout shift; product generally ranges from between 10-35 pounds and up to between approximately 60 and 90 pounds, depending on the location Company description 
Performance Foodservice, PFG’s broadline distributor, maintains a unique relationship with a variety of local customers, including independent restaurants and hotels, healthcare facilities, schools, and quick-service eateries. A team of sales reps, chefs, consultants, and other experts builds close relationships with customers — providing advice on improving operations, menu development, product selection, and operational strategies. JOB TITLE: Class B Route Delivery Driver

PAY: $34.00/hr

REPORTS TO: Service Center Manager
DIRECT REPORTS: No
LOCATION: Eagan, MN
JOB SUMMARY
CrossCountry Freight Solutions is in search of Class B drivers with a passion for customer service and a safety-first mindset to join our dynamic team. The CDL B position is a Route Delivery Driver position in which you will operate a Company motor vehicle to transfer freight safely and efficiently to and from specified locations by a specified time. This position unloads, sorts, palletizes, and reloads a wide variety of freight, manually or with the aid of a mechanical device. Completes all paperwork required by government regulations and Company procedures/policies.
ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES
Conduct pre-trip and post-trip vehicle inspections
Delivers and/or picks up freight to/from customer locations and/or a terminal as instructed by dispatch or the immediate supervisor
Ensures all shipping documentation is available for DOT inspection and appropriate paperwork accompanies the shipment to the delivery point
Loads and/or unloads a wide variety of freight onto and off a company motor vehicle, at customer locations and at the terminal, with or without mechanical assistance depending on the size of freight
JOB SPECIFICATIONS
Skills & Knowledge
Valid Class B CDL
At least 21 years of age
1 year of commercial driving experience
No DUI’s or DWI’s (in the past 3 years)
No more than 3 traffic violations (in past 3 years)
Must have Hazmat and Tanker endorsements or be willing to obtain - renewals reimbursable
Physical Demands
Must be able to frequently enter and exit the cab of a commercial vehicle.
Must be able to safely maneuver freight/pallets weighing up to 2,500 pounds onto a dolly or cart with a force of up to 130 pounds with mechanical aid in various environments/conditions.
Must be able to carry freight weighing up to 40 pounds for a distance of up to 20 feet.
Must be able to hook and unhook various commercial combinations, to manually lower and raise landing gear, to operate fifth wheel release levers, to lock and release pintle-hooks, to attach and release safety chains, to open and close cargo doors, to climb into and out of vehicles, and to fuel and check oil/coolant levels of vehicles.
BENEFITS
Local, Home Daily

title: CDL-A Regional Driver- 90K+/YEAR-5 days on, 2 days off- HOME WKNDS
body:
$80,000–$95,000/year | 5 Days Out / 2 Days Home | Weekly Pay | New Trucks
White Pine Freight LLC is hiring Class A CDL drivers for our Amazon Freight Partner operation based in Shakopee, Minnesota.
We're a locally owned transportation company hauling freight exclusively within Amazon's transportation network. You'll drive new Amazon-branded sleeper tractors, hauling no-touch, drop-and-hook freight on predictable regional routes.
The Schedule
5 days out. 2 days home.
You'll complete one 5-day regional route each week:
Spend 4 nights in the sleeper
Return home at the end of your 5-day route
Spend 3 nights at home
Then head out for your next route
You'll work 60–70 hours over the 5-day route.
That means four nights away and three nights home every week — a chance to put in serious hours and earn strong money without the traditional OTR schedule of being gone for weeks at a time.
The Pay
$80,000–$95,000 per year.
These are high-hour routes, and the earning opportunity reflects it.
Drivers work 60–70 hours during each 5-day route
Expected annual earnings of $80,000–$95,000
Paid weekly
Consistent, year-round Amazon freight
If you're looking to maximize your earnings while still getting home every week, this is the higher-earning route option at White Pine Freight.
Why Drive With White Pine Freight?
Get home every week. You'll spend four nights on the road, then three nights at home
Drive new equipment. You'll operate new Amazon-branded sleeper tractors designed for the type of regional work you'll be doing.
No-touch means no-touch. Our freight is drop-and-hook. You won't be loading boxes, unloading trailers, or making residential deliveries.
Run predictable freight. We operate exclusively within Amazon's transportation network, giving drivers consistent routes and reliable freight.
Work for a small, locally owned company. You'll have direct access to White Pine Freight leadership and be treated like a professional — not a number in a fleet of thousands.
Grow with us. We're building White Pine Freight from the ground up, and the drivers who join early will help shape the company we're becoming.
Benefits
Health insurance to help protect you and your family.
401(k) to help you build for the future.
Paid time off so you can take time away from work when you need it.
Paid sick time for those days when life doesn't go according to plan.
Weekly pay so you're not waiting two or three weeks between checks.
New, professionally maintained equipment so you can focus on driving rather than fighting old trucks.
What You'll Do
Drive safely and professionally. Safety comes first — for you, for the public, and for everyone working around the truck.
Complete 5-day regional routes within Amazon's transportation network and return home at the end of each route.
Move drop-and-hook freight between Amazon facilities without loading or unloading trailers.
Take care of your equipment by completing required inspections and reporting issues before they become bigger problems.
Communicate clearly with operations when routes change, delays happen, or you need support.
Represent White Pine Freight professionally at Amazon facilities, on the road, and everywhere our trucks go.
What You Need
Valid Class A CDL
Ability to meet DOT driver qualification requirements
Safe driving record
Comfort spending four nights per week in a sleeper tractor
Reliability and professionalism
A safety-first mindset
About White Pine Freight
White Pine Freight LLC is a locally owned Amazon Freight Partner based in Shakopee, Minnesota.
We're building a transportation company where professional drivers can do good work, operate quality equipment, earn a strong living, and be treated with respect.
Our culture is built around three expectations:
Responsible. Accountable. Proud.

The CDL-B Driver is responsible for driving a tractor trailer or straight truck on intrastate and interstate local, over-the-road (OTR), shuttle, and overnight and drive and drop routes for the purpose of delivering and/or unloading food and food related products to customers in a safe and timely manner and in accordance with Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations. title: Can't afford dues & fees? Keep your license active with NO MLS FEES
body:
As a licensed Real Estate Agent, we are responsible to generate our own income and pay our own expenses. 
Sometimes life priorities shift (or the market!) and the result is:
 You expect to have more transactions in the future, but just haven't had many deals in the last year or two.
 You had to start working another job.
 You don't have the time and energy to dedicate to prospecting for new clients.
 With all the NAR lawsuit changes and the shifting market, you aren't making enough in commission to justify the expenses.
 You love real estate, but the pressure to prospect and produce as a full-time agent isn't working for you.
 You want to retire, but can't completely step away from the business and lose all your income.
 You can't afford to pay your association dues & MLS fees but don't want to lose the license you worked so hard to obtain.
 If any of these points resonate with you, a referral-only brokerage might be a great option! You can keep your license active with Commerce and collect referral fee income, but you aren't required to pay MLS fees or association dues! You can transfer back to an active-selling agent at any time.

title: Software Developer
body:
Apply Now Description Leidos is seeking Software Developers to join the Air Traffic Business Area within the Homeland Sector, supporting the development of next-generation flight service and air traffic systems. This work aligns with the FAA’s broader initiative to modernize legacy flight service capabilities, replacing aging infrastructure with scalable, cloud-based platforms designed to improve safety and operational efficiency—particularly in remote and high-dependency aviation environments. These efforts focus on delivering mission-critical, future-ready solutions that provide safety-critical flight services to the pilot community. 
 As a member of a Scaled Agile software development organization, you will contribute to the technical execution of a program that integrates proven, globally deployed technologies with modern cloud-native capabilities. You will work alongside cross-functional teams and technical leaders to deliver predictable outcomes in a highly regulated, safety-critical environment.  
 In this position, you will design and implement software solutions independently while working closely with systems engineering, product delivery, and DevSecOps teams. The primary focus is on developing containerized applications within an  Agile/SAFe environment.  This position supports government programs and requires the ability to  obtain and maintain a favorable Public Trust investigation. 
 Primary Responsibilities: 
 Responsible for software development activities both individually and as a member of a team including writing, testing, debugging, and maintaining source code within an Agile environment. Actively participate in daily stand-ups, Release Planning, and other related team activities. Write and execute unit and functional tests. Troubleshoot and participate in the resolution of technical issues in lab and operational environments. Provide support as needed for system engineering, test engineering, and system owner teams. 
 Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related field with 2-4 years of relevant experience or a Master’s degree with less than 2 years of experience.                                                            Experience with Java programming language Experience with React Experience with Web development and commonly used front-end tools and languages (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) Experience with Linux Experience with version control systems such as Git or Subversion Experience with common development tools and IDEs (Eclipse, VS Code, etc.) Knowledge of AI-assisted software development tools and workflows (i.e. Claude Code, Codex, etc.) Knowledge of Cloud-based systems Knowledge of unit testing tools such as Junit and Mockito Understanding of sound software development principles and practices Ability to plan and prioritize personal tasking and be able to communicate effectively verbally and in writing Independent thinker, capable of performing high quality work, both independently and with a team in a fast-moving environment Ability to obtain SF-85 Public Trust suitability determination US citizenship required 
 Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of or experience working within the Agile/SAFe framework Knowledge of or experience with RESTful API, JSON, XML, XSD Knowledge of or experience with Spring Framework, Spring Security, and Spring Boot Knowledge of or experience with Python programming language Knowledge of or experience with Ansible playbooks and YAML Knowledge of or experience with Linux shell scripting Knowledge of DevSecOps practices and CI/CD pipelines Knowledge of or experience with MongoDB Knowledge of air traffic control and flight services

title: Senior Consultant - Application Development (Food)
body:
Apply Now Cargill is committed to providing food and agricultural solutions to nourish the world in a safe, responsible, and sustainable way. Sitting at the heart of the supply chain, we partner with farmers and customers to source, make and deliver products that are vital for living. 
Our 155,000 team members innovate with purpose, providing customers with life’s essentials so businesses can grow, communities prosper, and consumers live well. With over 160 years of experience as a family company, we look ahead while remaining true to our values. We put people first. We reach higher. We do the right thing—today and for generations to come. Job Purpose and Impact The Senior Consultant – Application Development is a senior individual contributor within the Digital Technology and Data team responsible for Salesforce Data 360 engineering and operations. This role enables the trusted commercial data platform that fuels AI-powered seller, service, and customer experiences. The role designs, configures, integrates, automates, secures, monitors, and continuously improves Salesforce Data 360 capabilities supporting Food CRM and Agentforce use cases. This role owns complex platform capabilities across data ingestion, data modeling, identity resolution, harmonization, Data Spaces, governed data access, activation, deployment automation, observability, reliability, and consumption management. The engineer partners with product teams, data owners, architects, security, privacy, finance, and Salesforce engineering teams to ensure Data 360 is reliable, secure, cost-effective, and aligned with measurable Food business outcomes. Key Accountabilities DATA 360 PLATFORM: Design, configure, integrate, automate, and operate Salesforce Data 360 capabilities, including Data Streams, Data Lake Objects, Data Model Objects, Data Spaces, identity resolution, calculated insights, segmentation, activation, and data actions.  SALESFORCE DATA MODELING & QUALITY: Define maintainable commercial data models and engineer controls for completeness, duplication, timeliness, referential integrity, identity matching, reconciliation, and source-system exceptions.  INTEGRATION ENGINEERING: Build and support governed batch, API, event-driven, streaming, and federated or zero-copy integration patterns across Salesforce CRM, SAP, Microsoft 365, cloud data platforms, and enterprise services.  PLATFORM AUTOMATION & DEVOPS: Treat platform metadata and configuration as governed assets using source control, peer review, automated testing, CI/CD, environment promotion, release controls, and rollback.  SECURITY, PRIVACY & GOVERNANCE: Implement least-privilege access, Data Spaces, tags, classifications, permission sets, object and field policies, audit controls, lineage, consent, retention, and separation of duties.  RELIABILITY & OPERATIONS: Establish service measures, monitoring, alerting, runbooks, root-cause analysis, replay, recovery, incident response, and preventive improvements for a business-critical platform.  CONSUMPTION & FINOPS: Monitor and forecast Data 360 and Agentforce credit consumption, define usage thresholds and alerts, attribute cost by product or business domain, and recommend engineering optimizations based on cost, quality, and business value.  AI & AGENTFORCE ENABLEMENT: Prepare governed structured and unstructured context for AI use cases and partner with Agentforce engineers on grounding, permissions, action boundaries, evaluation, observability, and human approval requirements.  TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP: Independently lead complex platform initiatives, document architecture decisions and trade-offs, coach engineers, review technical work, and influence platform standards and operating practices.  Qualifications At least four years of relevant experience in platform engineering, data engineering, application development, integration engineering, or enterprise data-platform operations.  Hands-on experience implementing or operating Salesforce Data 360, Salesforce Data Cloud, a customer data platform, or a comparable enterprise cloud data platform.  Experience with data ingestion, data modeling, identity resolution, harmonization, data quality, APIs, and batch or streaming integration.  Advanced SQL skills and experience troubleshooting complex data pipelines, integrations, mappings, and reconciliation issues.  Experience with DevOps practices including source control, peer review, automated testing, CI/CD, environment management, monitoring, and rollback.  Experience implementing data-security, privacy, permission, audit, lineage, and governance controls.  Experience supporting a production platform through incidents, root-cause analysis, monitoring, recovery, and continuous reliability improvement.  Experience estimating, monitoring, forecasting, or optimizing consumption-based cloud-platform costs.  Preferred Qualifications: Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant certification. Salesforce Platform Developer I, Salesforce Administrator, Integration Architect, MuleSoft, or Agentforce certification.  Experience with Data 360 Data Spaces, Data Cloud One, zero-copy data access, calculated insights, activations, data actions, packaging, and data kits.  Experience with Digital Wallets, FinOps, consumption allocation, forecasting, usage thresholds, rate limits, or cost optimization.  #HiPo Compensation Data The expected salary for this position is $100,000 - $140,000.  Compensation varies depending on a wide array of factors including but not limited to the specific location, certifications, education, and level of experience. The disclosed range estimate may be adjusted for any applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. This position is eligible for a discretionary incentive award. The incentive award amount is dependent upon company performance and your personal performance.  At Cargill we put people first.  As part of your overall rewards, we offer a comprehensive benefit program including medical and/or other benefits dependent on the position offered and hours worked. Visit: https://www.cargill.com/page/my-health/mh-health-and-wellnessto learn more (subject to certain collective bargaining agreements for Union positions) .  Minnesota Sick and Safe Leave accruals of one hour for every 30 worked, up to 48 hours per calendar year unless otherwise provided by law Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Vet. Apply Now

 Preferred Qualifications Experience with Java, Python, React, and scripting languages Knowledge of AI-assisted development workflows and tools (i.e. Claude Code, Codex, etc.) Knowledge of DevSecOps practices and CI/CD pipelines Knowledge of air traffic control systems, general aviation, and/or flight services Practical knowledge of FAA/DoD systems, technical policies, standards and orders Experience with leveraging requirement-management tools (CAMEO, DOORS, Jama, Jira with traceability plugins, etc.) and documentation platforms that support linking, reviews, and exportable RTMs
